You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
Clinical history (case record; may contain prior observations):
age: 56
gender: female
history: A 56-year-old female patient complaining of cough and dyspnoea for many weeks. No complaints of weight loss. She was a heavy smoker and had chickenpox at 33 years.Chest radiograph (Fig. 1) was performed followed by thoracic CT examination (Fig. 2).

Based solely on the analysis of the chest radiograph (Figure 1), which of the following findings is most consistent with the patient's condition and history, considering the differential diagnosis?  
A. Multiple small nodular opacities with a random distribution, some showing calcification, suggestive of healed varicella.  
B. Multiple cavitated nodules with ill-defined edges, indicating active tuberculosis.  
C. Large homogenous mass in the right perihilar region consistent with pleural effusion.  
D. Bilateral reticular shadowing indicative of pulmonary fibrosis.  
E. Single large calcified nodule in the left upper lobe suggesting pneumoconiosis.  
F. Diffuse alveolar infiltrates suggesting acute pulmonary edema.
